summary: Built and CI-verified a reusable external-clock latency harness over a bounded recent v3.30 worker sample. The reporter derives beacon→claim, claim→return and beacon→close from durable Git creation commits, defines explicit clock precedence/confidence, preserves missing close clocks as UNKNOWN, and separates observed wall intervals from active compute/waiting. Median observed beacon→claim was 673s and claim→return 239s for the three-worker sample; beacon→close had only one known value (1067s), with two UNKNOWN. No telemetry authority was created or promoted.
tests: PASS CI run 36655143411 derived the report from fetch-depth:0 Git history.
PASS three of three sample workers have known beacon→claim and claim→return external intervals.
PASS missing close clocks remain UNKNOWN/null; validation rejects UNKNOWN imputed as zero.
PASS clock precedence ranks GitHub server events above durable commit clocks and embedded artifact timestamps as diagnostic-only.
PASS report labels claim→return as observed wall interval rather than active compute and records concurrent-vs-sequential comparability limits.
unresolved: Only one sample worker had an explicit durable close/exam, so beacon→close coverage is 1/3.
Generic Git committer timestamps are durable but weaker than exact GitHub server-event timestamps; future scoreboard integration may substitute higher-confidence clocks where event IDs exist.
truth_boundary: Candidate observability harness only. No telemetry authority, scheduler change, performance promotion or Human Accepted state.
